title: introduce-stablepoint-temporal-canary-and-traffic-reverberation-shield
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Production rollouts show a class of slow, sustained latency drifts that evade percentile-based canaries and cause oscillatory cutovers when traffic patterns reverberate across cohorts. This PR adds a tempo-aware 'stablepoint' canary that tracks moving baselines across multiple horizons and a Traffic Reverberation Shield that quarantines traffic slices which amplify transient regressions. Key goals: 1) detect gradual upward trends before they breach SLO windows; 2) avoid noisy cutovers caused by reverberating traffic (e.g., users re-trying, fan-out amplification); 3) integrate with Redwood Console rollout policies for staged quarantine and measured fallback.

Summary of changes: Implements a multi-horizon confidence estimator that fuses rolling-window quantiles, exponentially-weighted mean shifts, and a bootstrap-derived trend score. Adds a probabilistic fingerprint sampler that groups requests by stable signal keys (user-agent + route + size bucket + subtle temporal bucketing) to isolate reverberant cohorts. Introduces a quarantine controller that marks cohorts for staged isolation and traffic throttling when they drive oscillatory signal amplification. Wires telemetry to existing perf-canary pipeline and adds dashboarding and alerts.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4021) - [x] Unit tests for estimator and sampler - [x] Integration tests with canary orchestrator (simulated traffic fixture) - [x] E2E canary run in perf-lab namespace - [x] Redwood Console UI hooks for quarantine policy - [x] Documentation (docs/perf/canary-stablepoint.md)

Why unique: Unlike percentile-fence canaries, Stablepoint uses tempo-aware baselines and cohort-level fingerprinting to avoid false positives from short-lived bursts. The reverberation shield enforces a quarantine cooldown and decay credit to prevent repeated oscillatory cutovers across rollouts.
